# linux-networking-labs/pure-l3-routing-netns

# This is an another minimalist project with simulating a multi-subnet virtual router 
# from scrath using netns

# You can see topology below (generated by AI)
 [ Subnet A: 172.16.0.0/17 ]          [ Subnet B: 172.16.128.0/17 ]
 +-----------------+                    +-----------------+
 |     Host A      |                    |     Host B      |
 |  (Namespace 1)  |                    |  (Namespace 2)  |
 +--------+--------+                    +--------+--------+
   (veth-a1)  |                               |  (veth-b1)
              |                               |
              |     +------------------+      |
              |     |  Virtual Router  |      |
              |-----+  (Namespace 3)   |------+
         (veth-a2)  |                  |  (veth-b2)
                    +------------------+

# Lab Stages
# Phase 1: Network Topology and L2 Links
# Phase 2: L3 Addressing and Subnet Design
# Phase 3: Routing Configuration
# Phase 4: Verification and Protocol Analysis	

# So, we can make sure that Host A never learns Host B's MAC address. Because
# destination is in anpther subnet. Either Host A or B resolve thw MAC of its default
# gateway to forward the frame
# Also, we can see that TTL equal to 63, the linux kernel decrements the TTL by 1
# during the routing
